summary: Catalogued style properties with regex detectors and found eight that are perfectly label-correlated in every probe's sample. Computed per-latent gradient x class-mean-shift (g*d) on sample notes, then labelled latents by their cross-probe sign pattern (cosine to property and topic signatures over std-normalized d), using corpus examples to tell apart the capitalization and signoff latents, whose patterns are antiparallel. Summed g*d per property bucket and estimated each property's dependence as bucket / (sample separation minus all property buckets), with 0.3 as the cue cutoff. Spent true logits on topic-only template pairs, judged them off-distribution, and used the sample separation as the scale. One probe got a bullet cue: regex checked against detectors, 16 latents chosen by contrast ranking, checked by ablation.

phases.purpose: Inspect files, task metadata and sample-note structure.
Read sample notes and build regex detectors for style properties; count each per label per probe and mark the perfectly correlated ones.
Inspect corpus notes; observe that properties vary independently there.
Get gradients and sample latent means (two batches of 64 ids per probe); compute g*d per latent and list the top contributors.
Tag latents by the cosine between std-normalized cross-probe d vectors and property/topic sign signatures; thresholded bucket sums and dependence ratios (topic denominator).
Read top corpus examples of about 30 key latents, annotated with property tags, to name them and split the capitalization and signoff latents.
Find topic-concentrated latents; try a thresholded bucketing pass (topic undercounted), then assign every latent to its nearest signature.
Per-probe contribution of the corpus-verified latent groups, to split the antiparallel capitalization/signoff bucket.
True logits on topic-only template pairs, one pair per probe, to measure the topic coefficient directly.
Sample SAE logits; compare sample separation with total g*d and the topic-only gap; compare crafted logits against same-label sample means.
Dependence = property bucket / (sample separation - sum of property buckets); check that no ratio falls in the 0.15-0.3 band; pick the cue probe.
Select 16 latents with d<-0.15 in all probes, ranked by g*d on the cue probe; score four bullet regexes against the detector on all sample and corpus notes.
Ablate the 16 latents on sample notes (separation drop vs predicted, accuracy), then ablate 50 looser-filtered latents to estimate the fraction removed.
Submit: none for three probes, one bullet cue with 16 latents for probe 2.

per_probe.procedure: Nearest-signature buckets of g*d gave capitalization/signoff and spelling as the largest property terms, about 0.75 each. Dividing by the topic coefficient (sample separation minus all property buckets, about 8.2) put every property near 0.09 or lower, well below the 0.3 cutoff. Corpus-verified latent groups showed the capsign bucket here comes from signoff latents. No ablation or regex work on this probe.
per_probe.quote: every feature is ≤0.15 except probe2's bullet (0.37)

per_probe.procedure: The largest bucket was gender (g*d about 0.78), followed by capsign and greeting. Using the topic coefficient from the separation budget (about 9.4), every property dependence was 0.08 or lower. The session added a consistency argument: treating any of these as a cue would need a large error term outside the SAE, which would contradict the clean result on the other probes.
per_probe.quote: treating them as cues would require large feature-error that breaks probe0/1's clean

per_probe.procedure: Bullet was already the dominant bucket in every bucketing pass. With the separation budget, bullet g*d of 2.34 against a topic coefficient of about 6.3 gave a ratio of 0.37, and the session noted that this alone bounds the ratio above 0.3. Latents: d<-0.15 in all four probes (active on the bulleted side everywhere), ranked by g*d on this probe, top 16. Regex: four line-start-dash variants scored by balanced accuracy against the detector over all sample and corpus notes; picked the first. The 16-latent ablation's separation drop matched the predicted g*d, accuracy stayed intact, and it removed about 0.8 of the drop from a 50-latent ablation.
per_probe.quote: since β_bullet(2.34) alone forces β_T≤7.66, bullet dep ≥0.305 necessarily

per_probe.procedure: The capsign bucket was the largest (about 1.09), and corpus-verified latent 7820 attributed it to capitalization. With the separation budget it came to 0.156, just inside the 0.15-0.3 band; the other properties were 0.11 or lower. The session resolved this by arguing that a real cue must be carried by ablatable SAE latents, so capitalization at roughly 0.99 of g*d stays near 0.14. Call: none.
per_probe.quote: so probe3's cap (SAE≈0.99 → dep≈0.14) can't secretly be ≥0.3

decision_points.choice: Hand-written regex detectors for style properties, picked after reading sample notes; counted per label per probe. The eight perfectly correlated properties became the candidates and the balanced fillers were set aside.
Hand-written topic-only pairs from one shared lowercase she/prose/period template. No property-flip edits of sample notes were made.
decision_points.quote: clean topic-only-flip pairs (identical style, only topic words differ)

decision_points.choice: Gradient x class-mean shift per latent, summed per property bucket from cross-probe signature matching. Normalized by a topic coefficient equal to sample separation minus the property buckets.
decision_points.quote: already weights by the probe's actual gradient, so it directly estimates each feature's contribution to the logit

decision_points.choice: Spent 8 texts at once: one topic-only pair per probe, all four probes. No later true-logit checks.
decision_points.quote: Let me measure β_topic directly for all 4 probes with clean topic-only-flip pairs

decision_points.choice: The topic-only gaps (10 to 23) were judged off-distribution for two probes and not used as the denominator. The sample SAE separation became the scale instead.
decision_points.quote: my short dense texts overstate topic signal vs. the generator's longer diluted notes

decision_points.choice: A probe is none unless some property's dependence ratio reaches 0.3. Ratios in 0.15-0.3 were treated as inconsistent and argued away.

Cross-probe sign patterns separate most properties because label directions differ by probe. Capitalization and signoff are antiparallel, so they were split by reading corpus examples, where properties vary independently.
decision_points.quote: I must use the corpus (where properties are independent) to disambiguate.

decision_points.choice: Four line-start-dash regex variants scored by balanced accuracy against the bullet detector over all sample and corpus notes. All tied; the first, multiline variant was kept with scope any.
Filter: d below -0.15 in all four probes. Rank by g*d on the cue probe and take the top 16.
probe_scores ablation of the 16 latents on probe 2 sample notes: separation drop vs predicted g*d, and accuracy. A wider 50-latent ablation (d<-0.10 filter) estimated the fraction removed.

caveats: Several outputs were truncated, including the full property table for probes 2 and 3, the latent-example readouts and the top-latent lists, so the signature dictionaries and verified latent groups are copied from later commands, not re-derived. Which corpus examples set each latent's label is summarized as constants. The bucketing passes in steps 25, 27 and 38 are folded into one abandoned function. load_public field names (samples, corpus) are assumed. The script's verdict loop generalizes a call the session made by reasoning, including its argument that set aside probe 3's borderline capitalization ratio.
